messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: kvcache-pool-42 on gpu-node-07 reported repeated OOM / container restarts (5 restarts in 10m). Metric: resident_kv_bytes trending +1.8GB/hour. Suspected paged-attention allocator fragmentation.
ashok: acked. I'm on it. Which customers hit this? any 5xxs seen upstream?
maria: sales-reported latency spikes for a couple of Dedicated customers (routes using model: redwood/gpt-open-16k). No 5xxs surfaced in edge, but internal retries increased. Grafana: https://grafana/redwood/d/kv-pool/gpu-node-07 (look at resident and slab_free_ratio).
taylor: saw CUDA driver errors at ~03:12:
```
[2026-03-15T03:12:08Z] cuda: cuMemAlloc failed: out of memory (700)
[2026-03-15T03:12:08Z] runtime: container restart (exit code 137)
```
Seems allocator requesting large contiguous pages when kv cache grows and attention pages get paged in.
devon: immediate mitigation options: lower KVCACHE_EVICT_THRESHOLD to 0.45, disable attention_paging for hot routes (env var ATTENTION_PAGING=false) OR fallback route to a smaller kv window model variant. Which do we want to try first?
jamal: doing a soft mitigation now: setting KVCACHE_EVICT_THRESHOLD=0.45 on pool-42 via ops-api and toggling a canary off for heavy route (route: /v1/generate/longcontext). Applying now...
eng-runtime-bot: config-change: KVCACHE_EVICT_THRESHOLD updated for pool-42 by jamal at 2026-03-15T03:18Z.
jamal: after applying eviction change I triggered a graceful restart of the affected container to force reclaim: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/serving-runtime-pool-42 -n prod`
taylor: after restart, node-07 still showing jitter but no new cuda OOMs in the last 6m. resident_kv_bytes dropped ~1.2GB after eviction pass. Good signal.
maria: customer impact update: two Dedicated tenants saw increased latency (p50 -> p95 jump) for ~8 minutes during the flare; no request errors returned. Recommend P2 incident and notify account owners. I'll open a brief customer note draft.
dashok: (typo, ashok) I mean ashok: tagging @oncall-next, please prepare to take handoff in ~45m. Also schedule `kvctl compact --node gpu-node-07 --window 24h` on maintenance window once stable.
devon: runbook step executed: kv-evict sweep ran and logged ~2.8M small slab frees. snippet:
```
[evict] freed_pages=2804320 reclaimed_bytes=1258291200 duration_ms=1782
```
kvctl compact queued, but compaction uses spare time; avoid while node is flapping.
taylor: noting one more pattern — fragmentation seems correlated with mixed model workloads (chat + long-gen) on same pool. Thinking we should pin long-gen to quantized model variant (lower kv retention) as medium-term fix.
jamal: quick rollback plan if we see regressions: revert threshold to 0.6 and re-enable attention_paging. Also prepared a canary route to divert 15% of traffic to fallback (quant-16k).
eng-runtime-bot: rollback-safe: canary created route `canary/quant-16k` at 15% by jamal.
maria: customer note sent to support and two AEs; flagged for postmortem.
ashok: next steps for handoff: 1) watch resident_kv_bytes on node-07 for 4 hours 2) run kvctl compact during low-load if resident doesn't continue down 3) if OOMs return, escalate to infra for node reprovision + gpu driver bump and consider draining pool and moving traffic.
oncall-next: I will take the midnight handoff at 04:00 UTC. Current status: stable after eviction, no new OOMs in 20m, compaction queued. I have the compact job ticket and can run it if stable for 1h. I'll also monitor driver error logs for any repeats.
maria: please attach timeline & logs to the incident ticket ID: INC-2026-0315-KV-07. I'll own the customer comms and postmortem.
jamal: leaving the runbook snippet here for next oncall:
```
- If OOMs spike: 1) set KVCACHE_EVICT_THRESHOLD=0.4 for pool 2) disable attention_paging for long routes 3) rollout restart affected runtime pods 4) create canary fallback route at 15% to quant variant
- If persistent fragmentation: schedule kvctl compact with --force-defrag during maintenance window
- If driver errors continue: escalate to infra (gpu-driver-team) to repro with `nvidia-smi dmon` capture
```
oncall-next: acknowledged. I'll follow this and escalate if needed. Leaving notes and handoff in the incident ticket.
incident-bot: Incident marked P2 at 2026-03-15T03:32Z (owner: maria).
ashok: thanks everyone. We'll do a postmortem to pin the allocator changes that reduce fragmentation. Handing off to oncall-next.
oncall-next: taking responsibility. monitoring until 08:00 UTC, will update ticket on any change.
